chunks: From him, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The one who slanders a foundling is flogged, and the one who slanders the son of al-mulāʿanah is flogged.

key_terms.ابْنِ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: the son connected to a case of mutual imprecation between spouses
key_terms.اللَّقِيطِ: the foundling; an abandoned child of unknown lineage
key_terms.قَاذِفُ: the slanderer; one who accuses another of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: is to be flogged; indicating the prescribed corporal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slandering a foundling or the son of al-mulāʿanah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the hadd punishment applies to one who falsely accuses a foundling and to one who falsely accuses the son born in the case of mutual imprecation. It underscores the protection of lineage, honor, and personal dignity in Islamic law.
